brief_points: Miriam has metastatic breast cancer with two biologies at once: luminal (HR+) and neuroendocrine (~80%). Spanish protocols only cover the first.
Without molecular rebiopsy and advanced panels, treatment is decided blind while the tumor evolves.
The campaign funds precision tests, second opinions, and a possible N-of-1 trial designed for her exact biology.
Every euro is documented. There are ways to help beyond money: clinical review, outreach, tech, or simply being here.

twofaces.title: One tumor, two faces
twofaces.intro: It is not one tumor: it is two biologies in the same body, and both must be treated at once.
twofaces.ne_sub: the one we need to know
twofaces.close2: Treating only one selects for the other.
twofaces.sr: Tumor schematic. Luminal breast, the known part: HR+ receptors, HER2 negative, an 11q13 amplicon (FGFR1 ×13, CCND1 ×20, FGF3/4/19 ×18) and an ESR1 mutation in ctDNA. Neuroendocrine differentiation (Cg/Syn in ~80% of cells), barely known: loss of RB1 (a brake that is being lost) and SSTR2 receptors, the PRRT target. Block one side and it escapes through the other; it must be treated as a whole.
twofaces.legend_rec: Receptors: targets to attack (HR and SSTR2).
twofaces.legend_amp: Amplifications: extra copies that push the tumor.
twofaces.legend_mut: Mutations: resistances the tumor builds to keep growing.
twofaces.legend_rb1: RB1: a brake that is being lost.
twofaces.legend_her2: HER2: a receptor she does not have (no target).
twofaces.legend_cgsyn: Cg · Syn: neuroendocrine granules (80% of the tumor).

entry_disclaimer.title: New molecular and imaging findings
entry_disclaimer.body: Liquid biopsies (April–May 2026) have revealed new alterations: ESR1 D538G (endocrine resistance) and RB1 mutations (a predictor of neuroendocrine transformation). The Ga-68 DOTATOC PET-CT confirms multiple bone metastases with somatostatin receptor subtype 2 (SSTR2) overexpression — a new therapeutic target via radioligand therapy (PRRT). The molecular profile has become more complex and reinforces the need to explore the neuroendocrine pathway in parallel with the breast (luminal) one.

home.s3_heading: What Spanish protocols don't cover, we cover.
home.s3_subheading: Spanish protocols only account for half of the tumor's biology: they're built for standard HR+ breast cancer, and Miriam's is not.
home.s3_p1: Histologically it is a luminal breast carcinoma (HR+/HER2−). But IHC detected ~80% neuroendocrine differentiation. That second biology is not part of the standard Spanish protocol.
home.s3_p2: Practical result: hormonal treatment covers the breast (luminal) component. The neuroendocrine component, with its own dynamics and targets, is left unaddressed.
home.s3_p3: The oncology team cannot prescribe off-protocol without solid evidence. Generating that evidence requires molecular rebiopsy, advanced panels and international review boards. None of this is funded by public healthcare for a low-frequency case.
home.s3_pet_paragraph: Gallium PET: multiple bone metastases with somatostatin receptor overexpression (subtype 2, SSTR2) and focal uptake in the right breast tail. The tumor expresses a target that breast protocols do not contemplate as standard, opening the radioligand path (PRRT).

ciencia.simple_body: No jargon: what's happening to Miriam, why her case is different, and what's needed now.
ciencia.simple_a1: A breast cancer that has spread to the bones. What's uncommon is that it behaves like two diseases at once: partly like a hormone-driven breast cancer, and largely like a different type (neuroendocrine). They're like two sides of the same tumor.
ciencia.simple_a2: Protocols treat it as an ordinary breast cancer and target only one of its two sides. The other is left untreated, and the tumor finds a way to keep advancing.
ciencia.simple_q3: Is there a way to target it?
ciencia.simple_a3: Yes. Analysis of the tumor has found specific "weak points" that could be treated with targeted therapies. These are promising hypotheses, not a guaranteed cure: that's why they must be confirmed before acting.
ciencia.simple_a4: A new biopsy with an advanced molecular analysis to confirm those weak points and design a treatment tailored to her. That's what the campaign funds.
ciencia.simple_more: A medical or science professional and want the detail, with biomarkers and tables? Switch to "For professionals" above.
ciencia.ai_summary_text: Miriam González ({age}) has metastatic BC-NED breast cancer (HR+/HER2− with ~80% neuroendocrine differentiation), FGFR1 ×13 amplification and SSTR2+ on Ga-68 PET. The next step is an advanced molecular rebiopsy. Donate: gofund.me/3e25cae99
ciencia.evidence_page_intro: Every hypothesis in this case is grounded in peer-reviewed literature and clinical trials. Here is the evidence behind the therapeutic axes, grouped by theme.
ciencia.evidence_hook_body: The peer-reviewed studies and clinical trials that back each hypothesis in the case —FGFR1, PRRT/SSTR, the neuroendocrine transformation and more— gathered on a dedicated page.
ciencia.proposed_panel_caption: Proposed bone rebiopsy protocol: component, method and core/format, targets and clinical implication
ciencia.axes_note: Hypotheses derived from the molecular profile, not a prescribed treatment. The advanced rebiopsy will confirm or rule them out before defining the N-of-1 strategy.
ciencia.goal_n_of_1_desc: A clinical trial with one patient. Therapeutic decisions are designed on the tumor's actual molecular profile, not on a generic HR+ average. The path: rebiopsy with advanced panel → review at WIN Consortium international MTB → molecularly-directed N-of-1 treatment.
ciencia.win_consortium_desc: WIN Consortium (Worldwide Innovative Network in Oncology) connects precision-oncology centers of excellence to design individualized diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
ciencia.win_consortium_precedent: A precedent: precision oncology decided on the patient's molecular data, not on the tumor's label.
ciencia.why_no_fit_guidelines: Why doesn't this tumor fit the protocols?
ciencia.why_no_fit_guidelines_text: On paper this is a {luminal} breast cancer (HR+/HER2−). Under the microscope, ~80% of the tumor shows neuroendocrine differentiation, with {fgfr1} and {ccnd1} amplification. Spanish protocols recommend treating it as standard luminal and ignoring the {neuroendocrino} component; yet the WHO has recognized breast neuroendocrine neoplasms as a distinct entity since its 2019 classification, and clinical literature shows this hybrid subtype ({bcned}) has worse prognosis and usually needs different strategies.
ciencia.thesis: The thesis: biology, not the organ of origin, should guide treatment.
ciencia.thesis_goal: Goal: an N-of-1 trial that sets a precedent for precision oncology in ultra-rare subtypes.
ciencia.updates_2026_subtitle: Results generated in 2026 that complement the 2024 primary-tissue profile.
ciencia.ctdna_what: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) from peripheral blood analyzed by NGS. A standard blood draw detects mutations, amplifications and clonal dynamics without a tissue biopsy. Especially useful in bone-only disease, where tissue is scarce or molecularly uninformative.
ciencia.imaging_intro: The tracer reveals an actionable target visible in vivo: the tumor expresses {sstr}, the target of {prrt}. Standard breast-cancer protocols do not consider this route.
ciencia.imaging_what: PET with the 68Ga-DOTATOC radiotracer, which binds mainly the somatostatin receptor subtype 2 (SSTR2). Visualizes in vivo which lesions express SSTR2 and could therefore respond to radioligand therapy (PRRT).
ciencia.article_fallback_notice: This article is not yet available in English. Showing the Spanish version.
ciencia.snapshot_intro: The essentials in ten seconds, before the molecular detail.
ciencia.snapshot_diagnosis: Infiltrating carcinoma (NST) with ~80% neuroendocrine differentiation (BC-NED) · luminal HR+/HER2− · premenopausal · dx January 2024
ciencia.snapshot_resistance: ESR1 D538G · RB1 loss (3 variants in ctDNA) · markers associated with CDK4/6i resistance
ciencia.snapshot_target: SSTR2+ on Ga-68 PET — target for radioligand therapy (PRRT)
ciencia.snapshot_status: ECOG 1 · no visceral involvement · ADELA and KATSIS-1 in screening · elacestrant in reserve (plan B) · PET-guided bone rebiopsy pending
ciencia.snapshot_grade: ER 95% · PR 5% · HER2 0 · Ki67 60% · G2 (Nottingham) · low TMB and MSI

ciencia.ctdna_dynamics_intro: The tumor isn’t static: ctDNA tracks its changes (VAF) across three plasma draws, with no biopsy needed.

team.title: The team
team.subtitle: An engineer investigating her own cancer in the open, an international team, and artificial intelligence —seeking the treatment that conventional oncology doesn't offer.
team.network_origin_body: A scientific and technological research association (biotech, AI, data). We're getting it ready. In the meantime, you can help the case:
notus_list: We do not promise cures. We document biological hypotheses and their real probabilities.
We do not use “fight” or “warrior” language. We talk biology, data and clinical decisions.
We do not replace the medical team. We add external analysis; clinical decisions are signed by Miriam's oncology team.
We do not publish clinical data without review. Transparency demands rigor, not speed.
We're not a perfect AI. The AI we use sometimes hallucinates — and the humans reviewing it do too. If you spot a typo, let us know.
team.how_it_formed: A team that formed on its own: medicine, science, AI and technology, each contributing from their own field, with a single goal —to let the tumor's biology guide the treatment. Clinical decisions always remain with Miriam's medical team.

historia.fallback_notice: This chapter is not yet available in English. Showing the Spanish version.
historia.pending_notice: This is the most personal part of the site, and it's being written by someone who knows Miriam closely: who she is beyond cancer, what she did, and why she does what she does. It'll be ready very soon. Meanwhile, you can follow the day-to-day on her social channels or get to know the case in The science.
historia.story_teaser_1: Three years ago, Miriam was working full-time as a software developer and creating content about technology. Within a matter of months, her life took a radical turn.
historia.story_teaser_2: It all began with back pain, physiotherapy sessions and GPs who couldn't find a solution. As the pain persisted and she wasn't getting answers, she decided to arrange an MRI scan herself. One Thursday in January 2024, she found the test results in her inbox: “probable vertebral metastases”. A couple of weeks later, the definitive diagnosis arrived: “Stage IV breast cancer with neuroendocrine differentiation”.
historia.story_teaser_3: For two years, Miriam has been rebuilding her life piece by piece with treatments that have given her time and peace of mind, but with an end date. In 2026, everything has moved forward at breakneck speed. What if these advances, combined with the specific nature of her cancer, opened doors that previously seemed closed?
historia.story_teaser_4: In this story, we want to tell you about Miriam's case, her journey and her daily routine so that you can truly understand what it means to live with stage 4 cancer.

collaborate.profile2_cta_caption: Secure payment. Receipt available. 100% to Miriam's case.
collaborate.profile3_title: You have an audience, community or media outlet
collaborate.profile3_text: The case needs to reach the right people: oncology, research or patients. Share the site or any social post. If you cover health, biotech or science, write to us and we'll send a press kit with verifiable data.
collaborate.profile3_cta_caption: Verified facts, coverage and a press kit for journalists.
collaborate.profile4_title: Background in software, AI, data or bioinformatics
collaborate.profile4_text: We are building an open pipeline around the case: literature ingestion, molecular profiling, trial matching and decision models. All code and non-sensitive data are public. Where to start:
collaborate.profile4_cta_caption: Open pipeline on GitHub. We'll bring you in.
collaborate.profile5_title: You are a patient or supporting someone in a similar situation
collaborate.profile5_text: You don't have to contribute anything: if it helps to know this case exists and is documented in the open, that already serves its purpose. And if you'd like to share yours or write to Miriam, you can do it by email or DM. Miriam or someone on the team tries to reply when they can.
collaborate.profile5_cta_caption: Miriam or someone on the team will try to reply.
collaborate.links_sub: If you don't know where to start, share the site. Getting the case in front of the right people —oncology, research or patients— is often the difference between finding a therapeutic target and not finding one.
collaborate.links_signature: — Miriam González's team · Beyond the Protocol

marcas.hero_subtitle: I'm an engineer and creator with an ultra-rare breast cancer: a profile that doesn't come twice. Over the coming months this story is going to have a lot of eyes on it, and I'd like to bring your brand onto it —not a one-day logo, but a presence that's felt and that lasts— to turn that attention into eyes on your brand. With full transparency, start to finish.
marcas.hero_context: And let me be clear from the start: I'm not asking you for a donation; I'm proposing a partnership. It's a charitable project, yes, but also a professional collaboration, and we treat it as such.
marcas.hero_tagline: // open to the right brands · there are people behind this, not an inbox
marcas.pilares_title: Four ways to put your brand {em}.
marcas.pilares_intro: The quickest to grasp, first. Four concrete ways to bring your brand in, designed so you can show them to your team as they are —if you have to pitch it to your boss, this is what you put in front of them— and pick the one that fits you best. They combine.

pilares_cards.title: Content co-creation
pilares_cards.what: We create native pieces together —reels, carousels, stories— that weave your product into a story people are already following.
pilares_cards.gain: Not an ad people skip: content the audience actually wants to see, with your brand inside.

pilares_cards.title: Product placement
pilares_cards.what: Your product, genuinely used and on camera, in my day to day (tech, travel/mobility, wellbeing).
pilares_cards.gain: Natural, credible presence, with no advertising script —genuinely seen, not read as an ad.

pilares_cards.title: Co-funded research
pilares_cards.what: «Research together with your brand»: you fund a concrete piece of the case —a test, a panel, a trip to Zurich— and we tell it with full transparency.
pilares_cards.gain: Your brand tied to real science and to an impact you can see and tell, not to a slogan.

pilares_cards.title: Mentions and branding
pilares_cards.what: Your logo on my profile and on the website (with real traffic) and a «thanks to your brand» at the end of every post, podcast shout-out style.
pilares_cards.gain: A constant presence in every post, not a one-off impression forgotten the next day.

marcas.pilares_dossier_line: Want it in writing to take to your team?
marcas.encajes_intro: Where your product meets my real life, that's where the collaboration feels authentic. And if there's already a brand from your sector, there's still room: that's what mentions are for.
marcas.audiencia_eyebrow: // the eyes you'll have on you
marcas.audiencia_frame: I won't bury you in charts: the brands that reach out do it for the media angle and to join something real, not for the exact size of the audience. If you want the fine breakdown, it's in the dossier.
marcas.movilizan_title: And when it counts, they show up
marcas.movilizan_p: This isn't an audience that just watches: when I ask for something concrete, it responds. In a recent campaign, that «give me a hand» turned into {b}.
marcas.movilizan_caption: A community that goes from scrolling to acting when it truly matters.
marcas.audiencia_cta_line: Can you see your brand in here? Write to me and we'll look at it together.
marcas.cta_p: Tell me what you do and, if it makes sense for both of us, we'll build it together: a collaboration works when it adds up for your brand and for this project at once. This isn't a form that gets lost: there are people behind it and we reply for real.
marcas.cta_podcast: And big initiatives are on the way to show everything behind this — the details are in the dossier.
marcas.cta_tagline: One of a kind. Like me.
marcas.popup_title: Bring your brand onto this showcase?
marcas.popup_text: This isn't an inbox that gets ignored: there are people behind it and we reply for real. Tell me who you are and we'll see how we fit.

expenses.title: Where the money goes
expenses.subtitle: Radical transparency: every euro, documented.
expenses.intro: Every euro raised is assigned to a concrete line item and documented here. This is the full breakdown of what the money can go to, in whatever order is needed.
expenses.cost_vs_goal: The first goal's €40,000 covers the first stage; the full range is funded in phases.
expenses.meta_description: Where every euro of Miriam's campaign goes: rebiopsy, sequencing and second opinions. Full transparency, with an expense report.
expenses.rebiopsy_intro: The centerpiece of the campaign is a single bone biopsy: everything current science allows is extracted from it today, and the rest is preserved so it can be analyzed for 10+ years. Its cost splits into two blocks.
expenses.rebiopsy_now_desc: Broad sequencing, expression, functional proteomics, single-cell and organoids on the freshly obtained tissue.
expenses.rebiopsy_bank_desc: Frozen, OCT and live tissue properly stored for new analyses as science advances.
expenses.rebiopsy_value: One procedure, not several: each preserved format avoids having to biopsy again in the future.
expenses.rebiopsy_note: Indicative figures, under review with the labs. Final amounts will be published in the monthly expense report.
expenses.faq_q1: How do I know the money goes to this?
expenses.faq_a1: Every euro is assigned to one of the line items above and will be documented in a monthly expense report we'll publish on this very page. Nothing is diverted outside the case.
expenses.faq_q2: What if more is raised than expected?
expenses.faq_a2: Funds follow the order of priorities: first the rebiopsy and treatment, then monitoring and the analyses the tumor comes to require. Any surplus is kept intact for the case's future medical needs.
expenses.faq_q3: Is donating safe? Is there a receipt?
expenses.faq_a3: Yes. Donations are processed through GoFundMe with secure payment, and you can request a receipt by getting in touch.
expenses.faq_q4: Can I help without donating money?
expenses.faq_a4: Absolutely. Sharing the site with the right people —oncology, research or patients— can be as decisive as a donation.
expenses.faq_a4_link: See all the ways to help
expenses.faq_help: Have another question or want a receipt?
expenses.note: The monthly expense report will be published here as soon as spending begins. We're working to show it as soon as possible.
expenses.phases_intro: The campaign is not a single lump sum: each phase unlocks the next clinical step. The first €40,000 goal covers the start; the full range is funded in stages.
expenses.phase1_desc: Bone extraction, broad sequencing, expression and first panels on fresh tissue (≈ €15,000–35,000).
expenses.phase2_desc: Frozen, OCT and live tissue stored for future analyses without re-biopsying (≈ €10,000–25,000).
expenses.phase3_desc: International second opinions, N-of-1 trial and monitoring as biology confirms.
